title: Sign-in: the welcome flight after a deliberate sign-in, and its Appearance setting
summary: After a person signs in (password, code, Google, GitHub) the photo travels to its place in the top bar with two short lines, in a full version (first sign-in of the day on a device, going to the default page) or a light one (later that day, or going somewhere in particular). A marker in the tab's session storage, consumed once, makes it play only in the tab that signed in and never on a refresh; after a full page load a curtain script in the document head covers the page until the flight takes over. One overlay in the root document, separate from onboarding's, which is untouched. A new Appearance preference, welcomeAnimation, joins the existing snapshot (on by default; saved snapshots without it read as on) and is stored with the other appearance choices in user metadata. One new server action records started, completed and skipped events in onboarding_events under separate event names, rate limited per person. No migration.
concurrencyRisk: None added. The flight is client state keyed to one tab; a second sign-in while one plays is refused by the host, and the marker is consumed when a flight starts. The telemetry action only inserts rows. The appearance snapshot keeps its existing newest-wins sync; the new field travels inside it.

rollback.strategy: Revert the commit. Nothing is stored apart from rows in onboarding_events (the existing retention job trims them) and the welcomeAnimation field inside the saved appearance snapshot, which older code ignores. Sign-in goes back to the plain move to the next page.

commands: npx playwright test --config tests/browser/playwright.config.ts signin-flight.spec.ts welcome-flight.spec.ts
